- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–8% from forecast 2–3 periods ahead.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15) and price is trending upward, model may underreact; increase forecast slightly (1–3%) to align with sentiment momentum.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; for periods 1–5, apply a 1–3% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.17 to -0.22), model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a 2–5% correction in the direction of sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, sentiment decay matters: if sentiment drops below 0.05 after 7 days, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
